metadata.title: European Stroke Organisation (ESO) and European Association of Neurosurgical Societies (EANS) guideline on stroke due to spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
top_takeaways: Strong evidence supports treating patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) on organised stroke units and implementing blood pressure lowering for secondary stroke prevention.
Strong evidence advises against the use of anti-inflammatory drugs outside of clinical trials for spontaneous ICH.

Weak evidence supports several specific interventions including acute blood pressure lowering, targeted surgical options (e.g., minimally invasive or decompressive surgery, cerebellar evacuation >15 mL), intraventricular therapies, intermittent pneumatic compression for DVT prophylaxis, secondary prevention antiplatelets, and integrated care bundles.

recommendations.statement: Patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage should be treated on organised stroke units.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage should be treated on organised stroke units.

recommendations.statement: Blood pressure lowering is recommended for the secondary prevention of stroke in patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage requiring secondary prevention
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Blood pressure lowering is recommended for the secondary prevention of stroke in patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.

recommendations.statement: Anti-inflammatory drugs should not be used in patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage outside of clinical trials.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Anti-inflammatory drugs should not be used in patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage outside of clinical trials.

recommendations.statement: Scores for predicting macrovascular causes underlying intracerebral haemorrhage may be used.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Scores for predicting macrovascular causes underlying intracerebral haemorrhage may be used.

recommendations.statement: Acute blood pressure lowering is suggested for patients with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Acute blood pressure lowering is suggested for patients with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.

recommendations.statement: Open surgery via craniotomy may be considered for supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage in selected patients.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with supratentorial spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Open surgery via craniotomy may be considered for supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage in selected patients.

recommendations.statement: Minimally invasive surgery is suggested for supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with supratentorial spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Minimally invasive surgery is suggested for supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage.

recommendations.statement: Decompressive surgery may be considered for deep supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with deep supratentorial spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Decompressive surgery may be considered for deep supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage.

recommendations.statement: Surgical evacuation of cerebellar intracerebral haemorrhage > 15 mL is suggested.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with cerebellar intracerebral haemorrhage > 15 mL
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Surgical evacuation of cerebellar intracerebral haemorrhage > 15 mL is suggested.

recommendations.statement: External ventricular drainage combined with intraventricular thrombolysis may be considered for patients with intraventricular extension.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with intracerebral haemorrhage and intraventricular extension
recommendations.verbatim_quote: External ventricular drainage combined with intraventricular thrombolysis may be considered for patients with intraventricular extension.

recommendations.statement: Minimally invasive surgical evacuation of intraventricular blood may be considered.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with intraventricular haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Minimally invasive surgical evacuation of intraventricular blood may be considered.

recommendations.statement: Intermittent pneumatic compression is suggested to prevent proximal deep vein thrombosis in patients with intracerebral haemorrhage.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Intermittent pneumatic compression is suggested to prevent proximal deep vein thrombosis in patients with intracerebral haemorrhage.

recommendations.statement: Antiplatelet therapy for a licensed indication may be considered for secondary prevention in patients with prior spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage and an indicated co-existing clinical condition
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Antiplatelet therapy for a licensed indication may be considered for secondary prevention in patients with prior spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage

recommendations.statement: Applying an integrated care bundle is suggested for patients with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Applying an integrated care bundle is suggested for patients with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.

recommendations.statement: Routine use of recombinant factor VIIa (rFVIIa) is not suggested in patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Routine use of recombinant factor VIIa (rFVIIa) is not suggested in patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.

recommendations.statement: Routine platelet transfusions are not suggested for antiplatelet-associated intracerebral haemorrhage.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with antiplatelet-associated spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Routine platelet transfusions are not suggested for antiplatelet-associated intracerebral haemorrhage.

recommendations.statement: General policies that limit active treatment within the first 24 hours of intracerebral haemorrhage onset are not suggested.
recommendations.target_population: Patients presenting within 24 hours of acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: General policies that limit active treatment within the first 24 hours of intracerebral haemorrhage onset are not suggested.

recommendations.statement: Temperature and glucose management applied as single measures (outside of structured care bundles) are not suggested.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Temperature and glucose management applied as single measures (outside of structured care bundles) are not suggested.

recommendations.statement: Routine prophylactic use of anti-seizure medicines is not suggested in patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage without documented seizures
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Routine prophylactic use of anti-seizure medicines is not suggested in patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.

recommendations.statement: Prophylactic use of physical/pharmacological temperature-lowering measures, prokinetic anti-emetics, and/or antibiotics is not suggested.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with acute spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Prophylactic use of physical/pharmacological temperature-lowering measures, prokinetic anti-emetics, and/or antibiotics is not suggested.
